newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher after short-covering bounce.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher after short-covering bounce.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures shook off bearish data in USDA's July crop report and managed to settle higher in a late short-covering rally, traders said.

KCBT wheat weakened early after USDA raised its estimate of U.S. wheat production. KCBT September wheat fell to $3.28 on news USDA pegged U.S. winter wheat production at 1.781 billion bushels, topping analysts' average projection of 1.687 billion.
But selling soon dried up, and by the midsession wheat had gained back some of the ground it lost early.

"This is a very impressive day -- a day that is encouraging additional short covering because we've been able to shake off bearish news and trade higher. Technically it's a very strong performance," a KCBT trader said shortly before the close while wheat was in the throes of its recovery.
KCBT wheat settled steady to 2-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with September up 1-3/4 cents at $3.36.
Traders said Farmers Commodities was a featured player, selling 2.5 million Sept but also buying one million Sept. E. D. & F. Man International bought 1.3 million Sept and sold one million Sept.
Cargill Investor Services bull-spread one million Sept/Dec at 13 cents and General Mills bear-spread 1.2 million Dec/Sept at 13 cents.
